title: Machine learning
audience: a college student in a computer science degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn the foundations of machine learning: data, features and tasks, linear regression, gradient descent, logistic regression, overfitting, regularization and the bias–variance trade-off, evaluation with held-out data, cross-validation and metrics, nearest neighbors, decision trees and ensembles, clustering, principal component analysis, neural networks and backpropagation, and responsible machine learning.
primary_reading: An Introduction to Statistical Learning, with Applications in Python (free PDF)

weeks.1: What machine learning is: data, features and tasks
weeks.5: Overfitting, regularization and the bias–variance trade-off
weeks.6: Evaluation: train/test splits, cross-validation and metrics
weeks.12: Deep learning in brief, and responsible machine learning

blocks.deliverable: Fit a regression model by hand and in code.
Implement gradient descent for logistic regression.
Compute precision, recall and a confusion matrix.
Week 7 midterm; build a small decision tree by hand.
Run k-means by hand on a small data set.
Implement the forward and backward pass of a tiny neural network.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: End-to-end machine learning study: on a supplied data set, explore the data, build and compare three models (one implemented from scratch), validate them properly, report metrics with their uncertainty, analyze errors and fairness across groups, and write a model card.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
